text:
incident-bot: ⚠️ P1 Alert: Canary rollout v2.3.1 -> runtime-pool us-west-2 showing p95 latency spike and increased kernel-fallback rate. Metric: kernel_fallback_rate >= 15% on canary nodes. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/paging.
ryan-oncall: I'm paged, looking. which customers on canary?
monitoring: canary slice traffic = 8% of prod. affected routes: /v1/generate (mostly long-context). p95 gone from 220ms -> 980ms over last 6m. error rate + 2.8pp.
jorge-eng-runtime: seeing repeated logs on canaries: \"kernel_select=fallback reason=kv_eviction_after_batching\". stack: runtime/kernel_selector.cpp:452.
sara-sre: suspicious — this looks like recent prefetch+batching heuristic change in v2.3.1. recommend kill-switch the new prefetch flag.
mike-release: I ramped canary to 10% ~9m ago. if that's the suspect we'll flip the feature flag and start rollback.
linda-support: CSMs flagged 3 customer tickets about slow responses (AcmeCorp, Finlytics). marking customer-impact.
anita-pm: please tag priority customers, I'll notify account owners and ops.
ryan-oncall: executing kill-switch now: POST https://flags.redwood/api/ff.prefetch_new_batch -> false (auth ok).
deploy-bot: Flag update accepted by control-plane. Propagating to canary pools (task id=deploy-4412345678-ffflip).
jorge-eng-runtime: also throttling canary traffic to 2% while we validate: `terraform apply -var canary_percent=2` done.
sara-sre: logs after flag flip: kernel_fallback entries dropping. preflag fallback_rate=18% -> now ~5% within 90s. p95 trending down.
mike-release: starting automated rollback of release/v2.3.1 -> v2.3.0 (canary and edge). deploy-bot: rollback started (job=rb-4412345678). ETA ~3m.
deploy-bot: Rollback complete for canary nodes. Control-plane reports 0/32 canary nodes on v2.3.1.
ryan-oncall: monitoring: p95 back to ~240ms, kernel_fallback ~=1.2%, error rate back to baseline.
linda-support: updated all 3 tickets, left note: \"We identified a canary rollout causing increased latency; temporary rollback performed; engineering monitoring.\"
anita-pm: notifying CSMs + exec summary to customers impacted.
jorge-eng-runtime: root cause hypothesis: batching+prefetch heuristic in v2.3.1 created larger contiguous cache churn -> kernel selector falling back to conservative kernel under pressure. Plan: reproduce locally with prefetch=on + heavy long-context load, then patch kernel selector heuristics and add safe thresholds.
sara-sre: created follow-up issue RWF-142: \"prefetch-batch kernel selector thrash on long contexts\". assigning to eng-runtime, severity-high.
mike-release: taking ownership of postmortem. timeline: -9m canary ramp, +2m p95 spike, +6m flag flip, +9m rollback complete. drafting now.
ryan-oncall: handoff: I'm staying on until stabilization window (30m). after that handoff to night-oncall @alex-night at 23:00 PST. please add any outstanding actions to the ticket.
incident-bot: Incident timeline note added. Pager cleared? not yet until 30m stable.
linda-support: customer comms template posted in #customer-comms.
jorge-eng-runtime: quick snippet of the suspicious log: ```[2026-03-17T18:12:34Z] kernel_select=fallback reason=kv_eviction_after_batching node=canary-7 pid=8421```
sara-sre: monitoring alerts muted for noisy metric, leaving critical on.
mike-release: TODOs: reproduce + patch, add canary gating for prefetch flag, add automated canary rollback on kernel_fallback thresholds.
anita-pm: will review postmortem and coordinate follow-up with product + QA + SRE.
ryan-oncall: final note for handoff: mitigations performed = flag flip, canary throttle, rollback; customer impact = degraded latency for small subset of canary traffic, 3 known tickets, no data loss. Handoff to @alex-night in 30m.
incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Pending follow-ups exist.
